Roadmap

Source: ROADMAP.md

Latent RSA model family

Goal: the procedure of the RSA package and of Schönbrodt, Testing fit patterns with polynomial regression models, as closely as possible in Mplus (MLR with XWITH).

Done (0.2.0):

  • Effects coding and pooled centering of the latent X and Y factors.
  • RSA_mplus() reads restricted models (rsa_model).
  • create_rsa_mplus_model(rsa_model =, start =) generates the 16 second-order models, including SRRR and SRSQD with the ridge parameters C, S, bM, and a4’.
  • fit_rsa_mplus_family() fits the family from one specification (by default RSA::RSA()’s 14 models, with start values from the full model) and keeps going when a model fails. compare_rsa_mplus_models() ranks the models by AICc (Akaike weights, evidence ratios) and adds the Satorra-Bentler scaled LRT against the full model from the MLR log-likelihoods and scaling factors, the latent R-square, and flags for failed or non-converged runs, Mplus messages, nested models that fit better, ridge lines that drift out of the data, and cd <= 0. Mplus reports no CFI or SRMR with XWITH. All 16 models fit in about 40 s at N = 400. reference runs the tests against another model.
  • Four models beyond the RSA package (addx2, addy2, noIA, a5zero).
  • identification = "invariance": a shared X/Y metric through scalar invariance (shared labels, no MODEL CONSTRAINT), which runs under Bayes, with free_intercepts for partial invariance, and fit_rsa_mplus_invariance() to test the assumption.
  • rsa_mplus_draws(): Monte Carlo intervals for the surface, ridge, and principal-axis parameters from the TECH3 covariance matrix.
  • rsa_mplus_supported_range(): the supported range of the LOC and LOIC from the model-implied latent distribution.

Next:

  1. Intervals for the derived parameters under Bayes, where the restricted models’ MODEL CONSTRAINT statements may not run (see Inference below).
  2. Plotting the observed region (the supported range, or points or a hull from FSCORES, which work with XWITH, or from scale means) and outlier screening (RSA’s Bollen-Jackman rule on scale means; Mplus Cook’s D and influence).
  3. A worked, executed example of the model family in the vignette (0.2.0 has the workflow with code only), and naming model_type = "si_lms" as RCSLMS (Cheung et al., 2021) in the documentation.
  4. Later: cubic models (CA, CL, RRCA, RRCL); an XWITH of a product works.

Not planned: the absolute-difference models (a step function of latent variables cannot be expressed in LMS) and the weak and strong fit patterns.

Inference for derived parameters

Mplus gives delta-method standard errors for NEW parameters. These are poor for ratios such as C, S, and the stationary point, where the RSA package bootstraps. Mplus refuses BOOTSTRAP with MLR. With ESTIMATOR = ML it works, but for the full latent model it takes about 0.7 s per draw at N = 300 (about 2 h for 10,000 draws per model). That is too compute-intensive and is not pursued.

Fallbacks, in order of preference:

  1. Monte Carlo CIs. Done in rsa_mplus_draws(): draw parameters from the asymptotic sampling distribution of the estimates (TECH3 covariance) and compute the derived parameters in R. No refitting is needed, so this is fast for any model.

  2. Bayes. ESTIMATOR = BAYES supports XWITH, and RSA_mplus() already reads its credibility intervals. To check: whether the restricted models’ MODEL CONSTRAINT statements run under Bayes, and how models are compared without AICc.

  3. Bootstrap with RCSLMS, only if the draws can run in parallel. The reliability-corrected single-indicator LMS of Cheung et al. (2021) is model_type = "si_lms", which always fixes the residual variances from the supplied reliabilities. Its measurement model is much smaller, but the bootstrap gains little. Timings on models/latent-rsa.dat (N = 300, Mplus 8.10):

    Latent RCSLMS
    Free parameters 33 12
    One MLR fit 2.0 s 0.4 s
    ML bootstrap, per draw 0.7 s 0.4 s

    The two-dimensional numerical integration over X and Y, which both share, dominates each draw, so 10,000 draws still take about 70 min per model. Mplus is not known to run bootstrap draws in parallel (not verified). Resampling in R with one Mplus process per draw would spread the draws over cores. Each process then starts Mplus once, but one RCSLMS fit including that start took 0.4 s. Eight processes might manage 10,000 draws in roughly 10 min; this is an untested estimate. The restricted models run with si_lms: SRRR gave S = 1.48, C = 0.22, and a4’ = -0.31, against 1.51, 0.23, and -0.31 in the latent model.
